title: Implementation of two-qubit Rydberg operations on neutral Rb-87 atoms in systems with different intermediate states
authors: I. V. Iukhnovets, O. V. Bychkova, I. B. Bobrov, A. P. Gordeev, M. Y. Goloshchapov, G. I. Struchalin, S. S. Straupe
abstract: This work presents an experimental setup for implementing two-qubit operations on neutral atoms ($^{87}$Rb) with the possibility of using two different Rydberg excitation schemes. One of them uses 5P$_{1/2}$ as the intermediate level and applies the second-stage beam locally to the addressed atoms. The second scheme uses the 6P$_{3/2}$ level; in this scheme, the particles to be entangled are moved to a separate zone through which both Rydberg beams pass. The advantages and limitations of both schemes are analyzed. Based on numerical modeling performed with a Julia package developed by the authors, it is demonstrated that the spatial configuration has a greater effect on quantum-operation fidelity than the choice of intermediate level. An experimental implementation of the scheme using the 6P$_{3/2}$ level is demonstrated, making it possible to achieve a two-qubit operation fidelity of 94%.
summary: The research details the experimental implementation of two-qubit quantum gates on $^{87}	ext{Rb}$ atoms by comparing two distinct Rydberg excitation schemes. The authors demonstrate that using a $6P_{3/2}$ intermediate level, coupled with a zoned architecture, yields high fidelity (94%) because it circumvents difficult beam focusing requirements inherent in alternative setups.
main_problem: The central goal is to experimentally implement high-fidelity two-qubit quantum gates on neutral Rubidium-87 atoms.
main_result: The authors successfully demonstrated a two-qubit operation fidelity of 94% using the $6P_{3/2}$ intermediate state scheme, which was shown to be superior to an alternative scheme involving the $5P_{1/2}$ level.
method: They utilized Rydberg blockade physics and implemented the Controlled-Z (CZ) gate via precise laser pulsing sequences following the Levine–Pichler method.
model_or_system: The system uses neutral $^{87}	ext{Rb}$ atoms trapped in optical tweezers, with qubits encoded in hyperfine ground states. Two schemes are compared: one using $5P_{1/2}$ and another using $6P_{3/2}$ as the intermediate excitation level.
key_observables: Two-qubit operation fidelity ($F$), measured via parity measurements on entangled states like $|\Phi^+angle$.
important_parameters: The choice of intermediate level, spatial configuration (zone separation), and laser parameters ($\lambda=420 	ext{ nm}$, $\lambda_2=1012 	ext{ nm}$).
main_assumptions: Numerical modeling suggests that the spatial configuration has a greater impact on fidelity than the specific choice of intermediate level. The $6P_{3/2}$ scheme is favored due to technological ease in generating high power at $1012 	ext{ nm}$.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the optical schemes for both excitation pathways (Scheme A and Scheme B) and show experimental sequences used to measure CZ gate fidelity and parity oscillations.
paper_structure: The paper compares two Rydberg excitation schemes ($5P_{1/2}$ vs $6P_{3/2}$) theoretically, analyzes their limitations based on scattering rates and beam profiles, presents numerical modeling results emphasizing spatial dependence, and concludes with the experimental demonstration of the higher-fidelity scheme using $6P_{3/2}$.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed comparison of physical implementations for quantum gates in neutral atoms, directly addressing practical engineering challenges (like beam focusing and intermediate state selection) that limit fidelity in current quantum hardware.
